activityGoals.name: Finding the Maximum Value in an Array
activityGoals.goalDescription: Write a program that finds the maximum value in an array.

commentList: We define array values to hold the specified numbers. We initialize the array by separating elements with a comma and enclosing the collection in braces { }.

commentList: We need variable maxValue to store the maximum value of the array. We initialize this variable by the first value in the array because we initially assume that the first value is the maximum.

lineList.content: //Step 3: Iterate through the remaining values in the array and decide which one is the maximum value

commentList: We use a for loop to iterate over the remaining array indexes and search for the maximum value. We need the array indexes to start at 1 with every integer number up to but not including the array length.

In the first part of the loop header, we define a control variable i and initialize it to 1. In the second part of the loop header, we test whether the control variable has reached the termination threshold. The loop is repeated if the control variable is less than the number of the elements in the array and terminates when the control variable reaches the array length. We can get the number of elements in the array by using the values.length expression. In the third part of the loop header, we increment the control variable by 1 after each iteration of the loop.
Note that the first part is executed once before the loop starts, the second part is executed before each iteration, and the third part is executed after each iteration of the loop.
Also note that the increment operator (++) adds 1 to the value of variable i and the result is stored back into the variable i. Therefore, it is functionally equivalent to the statement i = i + 1.

commentList: We need to compare the value at the index i of the array with the maximum value stored in variable maxValue. If the value at that index is larger than the maximum value, then we need to set the maximum value to the value of the element at index i.
